name: Leibniz’s differential calculus
summary: Leibniz devised the dx-and-integral notation and rules for finding tangents and rates of change, publishing in 1684 the calculus most mathematicians still write today.
description: A differential notation and operational rules for calculating tangents and rates of change, recorded in Leibniz’s manuscripts before the published 1684 account.
tier_reason: Reusable differential methods and notation support later mathematical analysis, physics and engineering across generations.
